title: The Polite Man
description: The name on the note keeps house eleven miles downriver. Go and look at him, and take note of everything he tells you, because he will tell you everything.

go_downriver.title: Greyhythe
go_downriver.objective: Ludo Corse keeps house at Greyhythe. Go and look at him.
go_downriver.journal: Ludo Corse, factor, of Greyhythe. Pyke says he has been down twice in three years, was perfectly civil both times, and paid on the day.

the_chair.title: The chair on your side of the desk
the_chair.objective: Sit down. Ask him whatever you like.
the_chair.journal: He answered the door himself, put me in the chair, and asked whether I had eaten. There is a chair on my side of the desk and it is worn through at the arms, which means a great many people have sat in it, which means a great many people have come here to ask him something.

asked_everything.title: Everything, honestly
asked_everything.journal: I asked him what he buys and he told me. I asked him who he buys it for and he told me. I asked him what the mark on the note was and he said it was the house's mark and had been since his grandfather. He did not lie once and I came out into the street knowing nothing I could say aloud to Reed. That is not an accident. That is a method, and he has been using it on better people than me for a long time.

asked_nothing.title: Nothing worth asking
asked_nothing.journal: I sat in the chair for a quarter of an hour and could not think of a question that would not have made me look like a fool. He was very kind about it. He said most people find the second visit easier.
